messages.subject: Threshold genetic distance
parts:
Dear Zhian,

I am using poppr to analysis the results of  a MLVA in bacteria and the final aim is basically dividing these bacteria into different clusters, according to their genetic distance.
I know that part of these bacteria have already been classified into 5 different biovars, but my dataset contains isolates not previously characterized.
My idea is to first use these already classified isolates to define a threshold distance below which they belong to the same cluster. After that, I want to apply this cutoff to the whole dataset and divide them into (possibly) more than 5 clusters. 

After clone-correct the dataset, I used mlg.filter with Bruvo's distance and the three different alghoritm to define a cutoff threshold to then collapse the MLGs into MLLs and here some questions have arisen:

1)  I used fraction set to 1, to calculate the cutoff among the whole threshold vector coming from filter_stats. Why there is even the possibility to set 0.5?
2)  Do MLLs correspond to clusters, as defined by clustering algorithms like the K-means or Hierarchical clustering? 
3)  By using the three different algorithms (nearest, farthest, UPGMA) I get obviously different cuffoff and thus, different MLLs (from a maximum of 18 to 12). Is there any reason why choosing one or another?
4)  Can I then use this cutoff value in a Hierarchical clustering like hclust? If I got it right, the height in the hclust dendrogram is not based on Bruvo's distance but on the cophenetic distance and thus I cannot used it there. 
     Is there another function where i can use this poppr threshold to define clusters?
5)  Or maybe my questions (and the aim) has already been satisfed by mlg.filters and thus, my question 2?

I hope I explain my self. There are too many options, too many discordant possibilties and results which confuse me a lot!

Silvia

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Threshold genetic distance
parts:
Hi Silvia,

I'm assuming your MLVA markers can be represented by a stepwise mutation model of tandem repeats.
1)  I used fraction set to 1, to calculate the cutoff among the whole threshold vector coming from filter_stats. Why there is even the possibility to set 0.5?
Because the function is designed to be flexible for any distance, not just Bruvo.
2)  Do MLLs correspond to clusters, as defined by clustering algorithms like the K-means or Hierarchical clustering?
The MLLs are clustered by hierarchical clustering as described in the second poppr paper (doi:10.3389/fgene.2015.00208).

3)  By using the three different algorithms (nearest, farthest, UPGMA) I get obviously different cuffoff and thus, different MLLs (from a maximum of 18 to 12). Is there any reason why choosing one or another?

I think this is really dependent on your system. The algorithms behave as mentioned in the second poppr paper (linked above). I made some animations showing their progress in the supplementary materials (mapped on to UPGMA trees):

Nearest: https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://github.com/grunwaldlab/supplementary-poppr-2.0/blob/master/images/upgma_nearest.html
UPGMA: https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://github.com/grunwaldlab/supplementary-poppr-2.0/blob/master/images/upgma_average.html
Farthest: https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://github.com/grunwaldlab/supplementary-poppr-2.0/blob/master/images/upgma_farthest.html

4)  Can I then use this cutoff value in a Hierarchical clustering like hclust? If I got it right, the height in the hclust dendrogram is not based on Bruvo's distance but on the cophenetic distance and thus I cannot used it there. 
     Is there another function where i can use this poppr threshold to define clusters?

If the hclust dendrogram is based off of Bruvo's distance then, yes, you can use that cutoff value (but only from the UPGMA algorithm). Another method to define clusters without using distance is to use adegenet::find.clusters() or adegenet::snapclust(). These use multivariate methods to assign populations.

Hope that helps,
Zhian
